```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
library(p8105.datasets)

set.seed(234)
```

## Simulated regression

```{r}
n_samp = 250

sim_df_const =
  tibble(
    x = rnorm(n_samp, 1, 1),
    error = rnorm(n_samp, 0, 1),
    y = 2 + 3 * x + error
  )

sim_df_nonconst =
  sim_df_const |> 
  mutate(
    error = error * .75 * x, #multiplied by x is the key thing here, where outcome variance depends on the predictor, which messes up the assumption for linear regression
    y = 2 + 3 * x + error
  )
```

Plot some data

```{r}
sim_df_const |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

sim_df_nonconst |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

```

Fit the regressions

Constant variance:
```{r}
sim_df_const |> 
  lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Nonconstant variance:
```{r}
sim_df_nonconst |> 
  lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Draw a bootstrap sample

Let's always write a little function

```{r}
draw_boot_sample = function(df) {
  
  sample_frac(df, replace = TRUE) # take a data point out of the bucket and write it down and put it back, so you can get the same point multiple times
  
}
```

Does this work

```{r}
sim_df_nonconst |> 
  draw_boot_sample() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

Draw a bunch of samples and analyze.

```{r}
boot_strap_df =
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample(sim_df_nonconst)),
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y ~ x, data = df)),
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  )
```

did this work??

```{r}
boot_strap_df |> 
  select(strap_number, results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  group_by(term) |> 
  summarize(
    mean_est = mean(estimate),
    se_est = sd(estimate)
  )
```

Look at the results more

```{r}
boot_strap_df |> 
  select(strap_number, strap_sample) |> 
  unnest(strap_sample) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, group = strap_number)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = .3) +
  geom_point(data = sim_df_nonconst, aes(group = NULL), alpha = .6)
```

Quick notes.

```{r}
boot_straps =
  sim_df_nonconst |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 1000)
```

If you do all this again, but with the constnat one, it'll give you the same results:

```{r}
boot_strap_c_df =
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample(sim_df_const)),
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y ~ x, data = df)),
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  )
```

did this work??

```{r}
boot_strap_c_df |> 
  select(strap_number, results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  group_by(term) |> 
  summarize(
    mean_est = mean(estimate),
    se_est = sd(estimate)
  )
```

Look at the results more

```{r}
boot_strap_c_df |> 
  select(strap_number, strap_sample) |> 
  unnest(strap_sample) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, group = strap_number)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = .3) +
  geom_point(data = sim_df_nonconst, aes(group = NULL), alpha = .6)
```

Quick notes.

```{r}
boot_straps_c =
  sim_df_const |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 1000)
```
